αἰγανέῃσιν: αἰγανέη — light javelin, hunting-spear; fem. dat. pl., epic -ῃσιν (= Attic -αις)
αἰδέομαι: αἰδέομαι — feel shame, be ashamed (to do something); pres. 1 sg. mid./dep., + inf.: ’I am ashamed’
αἰδοίη: αἰδοῖος — held in respect, revered; fem. nom. sg.
αἲ: αἴ (epic = εἰ) — if, would that; particle introducing a wish + opt. (αἲ γάρ ’would that’)
αὐτίκ: αὐτίκα (elided αὐτίκ’) — at once, immediately, forthwith; adv.
αὐτοὶ: αὐτός — self; intensive pron., masc. nom. pl.: ’themselves’ · also intensive in agreement with an unexpressed ’we’: ’we ourselves’ (αὐτοὶ βῆμεν ’we ourselves stepped out’) · also in agreement with an unexpressed ’you’: ’you yourselves’ (αὐτοὶ δ’ ὀτρύνεσθε ’and you yourselves rouse yourselves’)
αὐτοῦ: αὐτός — self; masc. gen. sg., intensive with a possessive (ἑὸν αὐτοῦ ’his own very own’): ’of himself’ · also the fixed adv. αὐτοῦ, ’there, on the spot, right here’ · also plain gen. sg. pronoun, unemphatic ’him’, governed by a preposition: ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ ’from him’ · also intensive with a noun, masc. gen. sg.: ’Alcinous himself’ (αὐτοῦ Ἀλκινόοιο) · also reflexive intensive gen. sg. after a personal pronoun: σέο τ’ αὐτοῦ ’and of yourself’ · also plain gen. sg. pronoun of a thing, ’from it’, after ἐκ (ἐκ δ’ αὐτοῦ πείρατ’ ἀνήφθω, of the mast) · also masc. gen. sg., intensive with a possessive sense, ’his own’: αὐτοῦ ἐνεύναιον ’his own bedding’, αὐτοῦ βώτορες ’his own herdsmen’ · also plain gen. sg. pronoun with a noun, ’his’: ὀστέα δ’ αὐτοῦ ’and his bones’ · also intensive gen. sg. with a demonstrative and noun: τοῦδ’ αὐτοῦ λυκάβαντος ’this very year’
αὐτὰρ: αὐτάρ — but, and then; epic conj. (= Attic δέ, ἀλλά)
αὖ: αὖ — again, in turn, back; adv., shorter form of αὖτε
αὖτε: αὖτε — again, in turn, on the other hand; adv.
βήτην: βαίνω — step, go; aor. 3 dual, unaugmented (= ἐβήτην): ’the two went’, said of several
βοσκομένη: βόσκω — feed, pasture; mid. graze; pres. part. mid. fem. nom. sg. (of the hind grazing)
βουλοίμην: βούλομαι — wish, prefer; pres. opt. 1 sg.: ‘I would wish’
βοὴν: βοή — shout, war-cry; fem. acc. sg. of respect: ‘good at the war-cry’ (βοὴν ἀγαθός) · also fem. acc. sg., direct object: ’shout’ (τεῦχε βοήν ’was raising a shout’)
βοῦν: βοῦς — ox, cow; acc. sg. (masc. ’ox’, fem. ’cow’)
γ: γε — at least, in fact, indeed; limiting/emphatic particle (elided γ’)
γέροντι: γέρων — old man; masc. dat. sg.
γέρων: γέρων — old man; masc. nom. sg.
γαίῃ: γαῖα — earth, ground; fem. dat. sg.
γαλαθηνοὺς: γαλαθηνός — milk-fed, suckling, still at the breast; epic compound adj., masc. acc. pl.
γε: γε — at least, in fact, indeed; limiting/emphatic particle
γενοίατο: γίγνομαι — become; aor. opt. 3 pl., epic -ατο (= Attic γένοιντο): ’would become’
γιγνώσκω: γιγνώσκω — come to know, recognise, understand; pres. 1 sg.: ’I know’
γνοίης: γιγνώσκω — come to know, recognise; aor. opt. 2 sg., potential after κε: ’you would come to know’
γύναι: γυνή — woman, wife; fem. voc. sg.: ’wife’ · also fem. voc. sg., plain address to a woman who is not a wife: ’woman’ (χαῖρε, γύναι ’be glad, woman’)
δή: δή — indeed, now, in fact; emphatic particle
δίσκοισιν: δίσκος — discus; masc. dat. pl., epic -οισιν (= Attic -οις), dat. of means: ’with discuses’
δαιτί: δαίς — feast, banquet; fem. dat. sg.
δαπέδῳ: δάπεδον — level ground, floor, pavement; neut. dat. sg. (τυκτῷ δαπέδῳ ’on the wrought, levelled floor’)
δαῖτ: δαίς — feast, meal; acc. sg., elided (δαῖτ’ = δαῖτα)
δείδια: δείδω — fear, be afraid; perf. with pres. sense, 1 sg. (= Attic δέδοικα): ’I fear’
δεξάμενος: δέχομαι — receive, take; aor. part. mid., masc. nom. sg.: ’having received’
δεῖπνον: δεῖπνον — meal, supper; neut. acc. sg. (περὶ δεῖπνον ’about the meal’)
δουρικλειτὸς: δουρικλειτός — famed for the spear; masc. nom. sg., epithet of Menelaus
δόμοισιν: δόμος — house, home; masc. dat. pl., epic -οισιν (= Attic -οις), plural for a single dwelling
δόμους: δόμος — house, hall; masc. acc. pl.: ’halls’ (plural for one dwelling)
δώμαθ: δῶμα — house, home; neut. acc. pl., elided (δώμαθ’ = δώματα before a rough breathing)
δὴ: δή — indeed, now, in fact; emphatic particle
δὸς: δίδωμι — give, grant; aor. imper. 2 sg.
δῖαν: δῖος — heavenly, divine, illustrious; fem. acc. sg. δῖαν, here extended to the sea (ἅλα δῖαν ’the heavenly brine’) rather than a hero · also of a place-name: Λακεδαίμονα δῖαν ’heavenly Lacedaemon’ · also of Dawn: Ἠῶ δῖαν ’heavenly Dawn’
δῖος: δῖος — heavenly, divine, illustrious; masc. nom. sg., epithet of heroes (= fem. δῖα)
δῶμα: δῶμα — house, hall, dwelling; acc. sg. · also nom. sg. (identical neut. form), subject of a verb: ’the house’
εἰπέμεν: εἶπον — say, tell; aor. inf., epic -έμεν (= Attic εἰπεῖν)
εἰρωτᾷς: εἰρωτάω (epic = ἐρωτάω) — ask, question; pres. 2 sg.
εἰς: εἰς — into, to; prep. + acc. · also εἰμί ’be’: pres. 2 sg., epic (= Attic εἶ): ’you are’ (τίς … εἰς; ’who are you?’) · also in the idiom εἰς ὅ (κε) ’until’: εἰς ὅ κεν … μιγήῃς ’until you mingle with’
εἰσήλυθεν: εἰσέρχομαι — go/come into, enter; epic aor. 3 sg. εἰσήλυθεν (= Attic εἰσῆλθεν): ’he came into’
εἴ: εἰ — if; conditional conj. (accented εἴ before a following enclitic, περ among them) · also introducing an indirect question, ‘whether’ (τίς δ’ οἶδ’ εἴ κέ ... ‘who knows whether’) · also with opt., of an aim in view: ’in case, to see if’ (εἴ τινά … λάβοι ’in case he might catch someone’) · also in ὡς εἴ τ’ + opt., ’as if’ · also in ὡς εἴ τε with no verb or optative expressed: ’as if’
εἴη: εἰμί — be; pres. opt. 3 sg.: ’it might be, he might be’; impersonal + inf.: ’it might be possible for him’ · also in a wish with a dat. of the person: ’may there be (for us)’ (εἴη μὲν νῦν νῶϊν … ἐδωδὴ ’may there be food for us two’) · also in a wish after εἰ γάρ, ’if only (all things) were’ · also in a fear clause after μή, ’lest it be (a god)’
εἴποιμι: εἶπον (aor. of λέγω/φημί) — say, tell; aor. opt. 1 sg., potential with ἄν: ’I would say’
εἴρετο: ἔρομαι (εἴρομαι) — ask, question; aor. 3 sg. mid., epic (= Attic ἤρετο): ’asked’
εἵματα: εἷμα — garment, clothing; neut. acc. pl. · also neut. nom. pl., subject: εἵματα γάρ ῥ’ ἐβάρυνε ’for the clothes weighed him down’
εἵνεκα: ἕνεκα — because of, for the sake of; prep. + gen., epic prothetic ε- (εἵνεκα)
εὐνήν: εὐνή — bed, bedding, marriage-bed; fem. acc. sg. · also of an animal’s lair, den (ἑὴν εἰσήλυθεν εὐνήν ’came into his own lair’, of the lion in the simile)
εὐνηθῆναι: εὐνάω — lay in bed; aor. pass. inf. εὐνηθῆναι, used in a middle sense: ’to lie (in bed)’
εὐρέα: εὐρύς — wide, broad; neut. acc. pl., agreeing with νῶτα ’broad backs’ (ἐπ’ εὐρέα νῶτα θαλάσσης ’over the broad back of the sea’) · also masc. acc. sg., epic by-form of εὐρύν, agreeing with a masc. noun (θαλάσσης εὐρέα κόλπον ’the sea’s broad bosom’)
εὔμαιος: Εὔμαιος — Eumaeus, the swineherd; masc. nom. sg.
ζεὺς: Ζεύς — Zeus, king of the gods; nom. sg.
ηὔδα: αὐδάω — speak, say; impf. 3 sg., augmented (αὐ- → ηὐ-)
θεοειδής: θεοειδής — godlike in form (θεός + εἶδος); masc. nom. sg.
θεοκλύμενος: Θεοκλύμενος — Theoclymenus, the seer, son of Polypheides; masc. nom. sg.
θρόνους: θρόνος — chair, seat of honour; acc. pl.
θυμὸν: θυμός — heart, spirit, soul; acc. sg. · also the life that leaves the body: ’life’ (μελιηδέα θυμὸν ἀπηύρα ’took away (my) honey-sweet life’)
κ: κε(ν) (elided κ’) — epic particle marking a conditioned or potential action (= Attic ἄν) · also + subj. in a general relative: ’whoever’ (ὃς δέ κ’ … ἵκηται ’whoever comes’) · also + opt., potential: ’would’ (καί κ’ ἐλθὼν … εἴποιμι ’and I would go and tell’) · also + aor. indic., unreal past: ’would have’ (καί νύ κ’ … ἔδυ ’and … would have set’) · also + fut. indic. in a main clause: ’will’ (τοὺς δέ κ’ … θέλξει ’and then … will enchant them’) · also + subj. in the protasis after εἰ: ’if ever’ (εἰ μέν κ’ αἰνήσωσι ’if they approve’)
κέν: κε(ν) — epic particle marking a conditioned or potential action (= Attic ἄν); accented before an enclitic · also + aor. indic., unreal past: κέν μοι … κατέχευας ’you would have poured on me’ · also + subj. in a main clause: ’may’ (καί κέν οἱ ὑπέρσχῃ χεῖρα ’and he may hold his hand over him’) · also + opt., potential: ’would’ (κέν μοι … εἴη ’would be mine’) · also + subj. in the protasis after αἴ: ’if perhaps’ (αἴ κέν τις … ὀρέξῃ ’if perhaps someone holds out’) · also + subj. in a temporal clause: ’whenever’ (ὅτε κέν … μεταλλῶσιν ’whenever they ask’) · also + opt., potential, in a clause with ὅ ’that’: ’might’ (ὅ κέν τις … ἀμύνοι ’that someone might defend’)
κακὰ: κακός — bad, evil; neut. acc. pl. · also neut. nom. pl., subject: κακὰ ἔργα ’bad deeds’
κακὸν: κακός — bad, evil; masc./neut. acc. sg.: ’by an evil (fate)’, inner acc. with μόρον · also neut. nom. sg., subject of an impersonal verb (τι … κακὸν … μελέτω ’let no evil thing be a care’) · also neut. acc. sg. as a plain substantive, direct object: ’harm, evil’ (κακὸν ἀλλοδαποῖσι φέροντες ’bringing harm to men of other lands’) · also neut. acc. sg., attributive with ἦμαρ: ’evil’ (κακὸν ἦμαρ ’the evil day’) · also masc. acc. sg., predicative: ’base, cowardly’ (κακὸν καὶ ἀνήνορα ’base and unmanned’) · also neut. acc. sg. attributive with πῆμα: ’evil’ (πῆμα κακὸν ’evil harm’) · also neut. nom. sg., predicate with an infinitive as subject: κακὸν … βάζειν ’(it is) bad to speak’ · also neut. acc. sg. governed by ἐς: ’into evil’ (ἐς κακὸν … βάλῃσθα) · also neut. acc. sg. subject of an infinitive: ’an evil’ (κακὸν ἔμμεναι ’that an evil is’) · also neut. nom. sg., subject of εἴη: ’evil’ (μή τι κακὸν … εἴη ’and may no evil be’) · also neut. acc. sg., attributive with ῥάκος: ’vile’ (ῥάκος ἄλλο κακὸν ’another, a vile rag’) · also neut. nom. sg., subject of a finite verb: ’an evil’ (ἐπεὶ κακὸν ἔμπεσεν οἴκῳ ’since an evil fell upon the house’) · also neut. nom. sg., predicate with γενοίμην: ’a bane, an evil (to them)’
καλυψοῦς: Καλυψώ — Calypso, a nymph; fem. gen. sg.
κατέθεντο: κατατίθημι — put down, stow away; aor. 3 pl. mid.: ’stowed’
κατέλεξα: καταλέγω — recount, tell in order; aor. 1 sg.: ’I told, recounted’
καταλέξω: καταλέγω — recount in full and in order; fut. 1 sg. or aor. subj. 1 sg. (the epic forms coincide): ’I will tell in full’
κατὰ: κατά — down, throughout, in; prep. + acc.; also as preverb in tmesis (κατὰ … ἤσθιον = κατήσθιον ’devoured’) · also ’according to, in conformity with’ (κατὰ μοῖραν ’according to what is fitting’) · also + acc., ’in quest of, after’ (κατὰ ληίδα ’in quest of plunder’) · also + gen., ’down from’ (κατὰ πετράων ’down from the rocks’) · also + gen., ’all over, throughout’ (κατὰ σπείους κέχυτο ’lay spread all over the cave’) · also + acc., of the part grasped: ’by’ (κατὰ νῶτα λαβών ’taking him by the back’) · also + acc., ’on account of, on the business of’ (κατὰ χρέος ’on business’) · also + gen., ’down in, within’ (κατὰ σπείους κοίλοιο δέδυκεν ’is sunk in the hollow cave’)
κε: κε(ν) — epic particle marking a conditioned or potential action (= Attic ἄν) · also + subj. after εἰς ὅ, ’until’ (εἰς ὅ κε … ἐποτρύνῃ ’until … urges on’) · also + subj. in a general relative: ’whoever’ (ὅς κε πίῃ) · also + subj. in a temporal clause: ’whenever, as soon as’ (ὅτε … κε θάνῃσιν; ἐπεί κε … λίπῃ) · also + subj. in a purpose clause after ὄφρα: ’so that’ (ὄφρα κε … ἀκούσῃς) · also + subj. in the protasis after εἰ: ’if ever’ (εἰ δέ κε λίσσηαι ’but if you beg’) · also + aor. indic., unreal past: ’would have’ (καὶ νύ κε … βάλεν ’and she would have hurled’) · also + subj. in a disjunctive statement of what may happen: ’may’ (ἤ κε θάνωμεν ’either we may die’) · also + opt., potential: ’would’ (καί κε … μαχοίμην ’I would fight’) · also + subj. in a relative clause of purpose: ’who are to’ (οἵ κε … ἀγγείλωσι ’who are to announce’)
κείνοισιν: κεῖνος (= Attic ἐκεῖνος) — that, yonder; demonstr. pron./adj., masc. dat. pl.: ’upon those men’
κελεύεις: κελεύω — bid, command, order; pres. 2 sg.
κεχάροντο: χαίρω — rejoice, be glad; redupl. aor. 3 pl., unaugmented: ’they rejoiced’
κεῖνος: κεῖνος — that, that one; demonstrative pron., epic (= Attic ἐκεῖνος); masc. nom. sg.
κλισμούς: κλισμός — chair, seat (lighter than the θρόνος); acc. pl.
κνημοὺς: κνημός — mountain slope, spur, ridge; masc. acc. pl.
κοιμήσασα: κοιμάω — lull to sleep, put to rest; aor. part. act. fem. nom. sg.: ’having lulled to rest’
κοῦροι: κοῦρος — young man, boy; nom. pl.
κρατέρ: κρατερός — mighty, strong, harsh; neut. acc. pl., elided (κρατέρ’ = κρατερά)
κρατεροῖο: κρατερός — strong, mighty; masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -οῦ)
κρατερόφρονος: κρατερόφρων — strong-minded, stout of heart (κρατερός + φρήν); adj., masc. gen. sg.
κρατερῶς: κρατερῶς — mightily, forcefully; adv. from κρατερός
κυδαλίμοισιν: κυδάλιμος — glorious, renowned; masc. dat. pl., epic -οισιν (= Attic -οις)
κὰδ: κατά (apocope κάδ before δ-) — down through, throughout; prep./preverb in tmesis: ’throughout the halls’ (κὰδ δώματα = κατὰ δώματα) · also a bare preverb in tmesis with a verb: κὰδ ... ἔβαλε = κατέβαλε ’threw down’
λέσβῳ: Λέσβος — Lesbos, an Aegean island; fem. dat. sg. (place where, ἐν Λέσβῳ)
λίσσεαι: λίσσομαι — beg, entreat, beseech; pres. 2 sg. mid., epic uncontracted (= Attic λίσσῃ)
λαερτιάδεω: Λαερτιάδης — son of Laertes; masc. gen. sg., epic -εω (= Attic -ου), a patronymic of Odysseus
λακεδαίμονα: Λακεδαίμων — Lacedaemon, the land in which Sparta lies; fem. acc. sg.
λαῶν: λαός — people, host; masc. gen. pl., governed by ἄνασσε ’was lord over’ · also gen. with a noun: ’of the people’ (ποιμένα λαῶν ’shepherd of the people’) · also governed by ἐκ: ἔκ ... λαῶν ’from the people’ · also partitive gen. after a relative: οἵ ... λαῶν ἡμετέρων ’those of our people who’ · also partitive gen. after an adjective of rank: πάντων ἀριδείκετε λαῶν ’most distinguished of all the people’ · also gen. governed by πρόσθεν: ’before (the city and) the people’
λευγαλέῳ: λευγαλέος — pitiful, sorry, miserable; masc. dat. sg.
λιπέσθαι: λείπω — leave; aor. mid. inf. λιπέσθαι: ’to be left behind’ (παῖδα λιπέσθαι ’that a son be left behind’)
λυγρὰ: λυγρός — grievous, baneful, miserable; neut. acc. pl. (grave, mid-clause form): ’grievous things’
μ: ἐγώ — I; encl. acc. sg., elided (μ’ = με): ’me’ · also = dat. μοι, elided before a vowel, with a dat. participle: ’to me’ (ἥ μ’ οἴῳ ἔρροντι συνήντετο, συναντάω + dat.)
μάλα: μάλα — very, very much, exceedingly; adv.
μάλιστα: μάλα — very, much; superl. adv. μάλιστα: ’most of all, especially’
μέδων: Μέδων — Medon, herald of Odysseus’s household; masc. nom. sg.
μέν: μέν — on the one hand; particle, often answered by δέ (the acute μέν is kept before a following enclitic; elsewhere μὲν) · also asseverative, = μήν ’truly, indeed’ (οὐ μέν ’not indeed’) · also μένω — stay, wait; pres. imper. 2 sg., elided (μέν’ = μένε): ’stay’
μένοντες: μένω — remain, wait, stay; pres. part. masc. nom. pl.: ’waiting’
μή: μή — not; negative particle (used with imperatives and subjunctives, unlike οὐ) · also introducing a negative purpose/fear clause with the optative in secondary sequence: μή ἑ λάθοι ’lest he should escape notice’ · also μή + fut. inf. after a verb of swearing/promising, negating its content: μή ... βουλευσέμεν ’that ... will not plan’ · also ’lest’ with the subj. after a primary verb (μή πώς ... χαλεπήνῃ ’lest he be harsh’) · also in a question expecting the answer ’no’, after ἦ: ἦ μή … φάσθ’ ἔμμεναι; ’surely you do not say … are?’ · also ’lest’ + subj. after a past verb of urging (κελόμην … μή … λάθηται ’I urged … lest he forget’) · also in a condition, ’if … not’ (εἰ … μή τίς σε βιάζεται) · also with an infinitive used as an imperative, a prohibition: μή μ’ … καταλείπειν ’do not leave me’ · also negating a purpose clause after ἵνα: ’so that … not’ (ἵνα μή τι … ἀλγήσετε ’so that you may not suffer’) · also with the optative, a negative wish: ’may … not’ (μή … ἀντιβολήσαις) · also ὡς ἂν μή + subj., negative purpose: ’so that … not’ (ὡς ἂν μή σε κατατρύχῃ ’so that he may not wear you out’)
μακαρίζοι: μακαρίζω — call blessed, congratulate; pres. opt. 3 sg., in a purpose clause after ὡς ἄν
μαντεύσομαι: μαντεύομαι — prophesy, divine (from μάντις); fut. 1 sg.
μεγάροιο: μέγαρον — hall; gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου)
μεγάροισι: μέγαρον — hall; dat. pl., epic -οισι (= Attic -οις)
μενέλαον: Μενέλαος — Menelaus, king of Sparta, brother of Agamemnon; acc. sg.
μενέλαος: Μενέλαος — Menelaus, king of Sparta, brother of Agamemnon; masc. nom. sg.
μετέειπε: μετεῖπον — speak among, address; aor. 3 sg., epic uncontracted, augment ἐ- kept (= Attic μετεῖπε)
μιν: μιν — him, her, it; epic encl. acc. pron. (= Attic αὐτόν/αὐτήν/αὐτό)
μοι: ἐγώ — I; encl. dat. sg.: ’to me, for me’ · also dat. of the person affected, ’from my …’ (μοι βλεφάρων ἐξέσσυτο ὕπνος ’sleep rushed out from my eyelids’) · also dat. of possession with εἰμί: ’who are mine’ (οἵ μοι ἔασιν ’who are mine’)
μόγησαν: μογέω — toil, suffer hardship; aor. 3 pl., unaugmented (= ἐμόγησαν)
μύθων: μῦθος — speech, word, thing said (not yet ’myth’ in Homer); gen. pl.
μύθῳ: μῦθος — word, speech, plea; masc. dat. sg.
μὲν: μέν — on the one hand; particle, often answered by δέ · also asseverative, = μήν ’truly, indeed’: οὐ μὲν δή ’surely not’
μῆλα: μῆλον — sheep, goat, flock-animal; neut. nom. pl.: ’the flocks’ · also neut. acc. pl. (same form), direct object: ἦγον ... μῆλα ’they led sheep’
μῦθον: μῦθος — word, speech, thing said; acc. sg. · also a plan, scheme agreed on (τοῖον...τελέωμεν μῦθον ’let us carry out this plan’)
νέον: νέος — new, young; neut. acc. sg. used adverbially: ’newly, for the first time’ · also masc. acc. sg., ’young’ (νέον ἄνδρα ’a young man’) · also neut. nom./acc. sg., ’new’ (οὔ τι νέον ’not a new one’, of a debt) · also adv., ’just now, a moment ago’ (νέον ἠὲ πάροιθεν ’just now than before’; νέον ἦσθα γέρων ’just now you were an old man’)
νέστορα: Νέστωρ — Nestor, king of Pylos; acc. sg.
ναιετάοντας: ναιετάω — dwell, be inhabited; pres. part. masc. acc. pl., epic uncontracted (contracted ναιετῶντας; prose says οἰκέω): ’inhabited’
νεβροὺς: νεβρός — fawn, young deer; masc./fem. acc. pl.
νεηγενέας: νεηγενής — newborn, newly-born (νέος + γίγνομαι); epic compound adj., masc./fem. acc. pl.
νεόμην: νέομαι — return, go home; impf. 1 sg., inceptive force: ’I set out for home’
νημερτής: νημερτής — unerring, infallible, truthful (νη- + ἁμαρτάνω); adj., masc. nom. sg., standing epithet of Proteus (γέρων ἅλιος νημερτής)
νηὸς: ναῦς — ship; gen. sg., epic νηός (= Attic νεώς)
νοέοντι: νοέω — perceive, understand; pres. part. act., masc. dat. sg., epic uncontracted (= Attic νοοῦντι): ’to one who understands’
νύμφης: νύμφη — nymph, young bride; fem. gen. sg.
νῆες: ναῦς — ship; fem. nom. pl., epic νῆες
νῶτα: νῶτον — back; neut. acc. pl. νῶτα, poetic image ’the broad back(s) of the sea’ · also ’back’ of a person: ’his back’ (ἥ οἱ νῶτα … ἄμπεχεν) · also the backs of animals: ’backs’ (ὀίων … νῶτα)
ξενίη: ξένιος — of a guest, of hospitality; fem. nom. sg., Ionic -η (= Attic ξενία): ’hospitable’ (or the noun ’hospitality’)
ξεῖν: ξεῖνος — stranger, guest-friend; voc. sg., elided (ξεῖν’ = ξεῖνε)
ξεῖνε: ξεῖνος — stranger, guest-friend (epic = Attic ξένος); voc. sg.
ξυλόχῳ: ξύλοχος — thicket, copse, lair; masc. dat. sg.
οἰωνὸν: οἰωνός — bird of omen, bird of prey; masc. acc. sg.
οἱ: οἱ — encl. dat. sg. pron. ’to/for him’ (very common) · also ὁ, ἡ, τό ’he, she, it’, masc. nom. pl. ’they’ (e.g. οἱ μὲν … οἱ δέ ’some … others’) · also encl. dat. sg. fem. ’to/for her’ (ἥ οἱ ὁμηλικίη ’who was of an age with her’) · also article-like with a numeral and noun, masc. nom. pl.: ’the’ (οἱ δὲ δύω σκόπελοι ’the two crags’) · also encl. dat. sg. of a thing, ’to/for it’ (δύω δέ τέ οἱ θύραι ’and it has two doors’) · also article-like with a noun, masc. nom. pl.: ’those, the’ (οἱ πέπλοι ’the robes’) · also dat. sg. of the giver with δέχομαι: ’from him’ (οἱ ἐδέξατο ’took from him’)
οἳ: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — who, which; relative pron., masc. nom. pl.
οἵ: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — who, which; relative pron., masc. nom. pl. · also encl. dat. sg. pron. ’to/for him’ (= οἱ, accented οἵ in this position) · also ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; masc. nom. pl. ’they’, demonstrative: οἵ γ’ ὑβρισταί ’are they violent?’
οἶδεν: οἶδα — know; perf. 3 sg. (with pres. sense): ’knows’
οἷός: οἷος — such as, of what sort; relative adj., masc. nom. sg., correlative with τοῖος: ’such as, as ... when’
οὐδ: οὐδέ (elided οὐδ’) — and not, nor, not even
οὐδέ: οὐδέ — and not, nor, not even; neg. conj.
οὐδέν: οὐδείς, οὐδεμία, οὐδέν — no one, nothing; neut. acc. sg.: ’nothing, no (word)’
οὐδόν: οὐδός — threshold; masc. acc. sg.: ’threshold (of old age)’, a figure for reaching it · also the literal threshold of a house (ὑπέρβη λάϊνον οὐδόν ’stepped over the stone threshold’)
οὐδὲ: οὐδέ — and not, nor, not even; neg. conj. (grave, mid-clause form)
οὐκ: οὐ — not; neg. adv., form before a vowel with smooth breathing (οὐχ before a rough breathing)
οὔ: οὐ — not; neg. adv., in a question expecting the answer ’yes’ · also the plain negative adverb in a declarative statement, with no question implied: ’not’
οὖρον: οὖρος — fair wind, following wind; masc. acc. sg. · also a different word, neut. ’furrow-stretch’, the length a pair of mules ploughs in one go (οὖρον … ἡμιόνοιιν); exact measure unknown · also a different word, οὖρος — warden, guardian (related to ὁράω ’see, watch’); masc. acc. sg. (οὐ … οὖρον … κατέλειπον ’I left no warden behind’)
οὗ: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — who, which; relative pron., masc. gen. sg.: ’whose’ (= Attic οὗ) · also neut. gen. sg. in ἐξ οὗ ’since, from the time when’ · also possessive ὅς, ἥ, ὅν: his own, her own; masc. gen. sg. agreeing with a noun (οὗ πατρὸς ’her own father’s’)
πάντες: πᾶς — all, every; masc. nom. pl.
πάντεσσι: πᾶς — all, every; masc. dat. pl., epic -εσσι (= Attic πᾶσι)
πάντοθεν: πάντοθεν — from all sides, on every side; adv.
πάρα: παρά — beside; πάρα (accent drawn back) stands for πάρεστι/πάρεισι ’is/are at hand, present’ · also prep. placed after its noun (anastrophe) · also adv. after its verb (anastrophe): ἐτίθει πάρα ’set beside’ (= παρετίθει)
πάροιθεν: πάροιθεν — before, formerly; adv. · also + gen., spatial: ’in front of, before’ (πάροιθεν Ὀδυσσῆος μεγάροιο ’in front of Odysseus’s hall’)
πάρος: πάρος — before, formerly; adv., with inf. like Attic πρίν · also a plain temporal adverb with a finite verb, not paired with an infinitive: ’formerly, in the past’ (αἳ πάρος ἦσαν ’who formerly were’)
πέμποιεν: πέμπω — send, convey, escort; pres. opt. 3 pl., potential in a relative clause of characteristic: ’who might convey’
πήρην: πήρη — wallet, beggar’s bag; fem. acc. sg.
πίονας: πίων — fat, rich; masc./fem. acc. pl. (fem. usually πίειρα)
παρὲξ: παρέξ — beside, past, beyond; adv./prep. + acc., here adverbial with εἴποιμι: ’say otherwise, speak beside the point’ · also adv. with ἐλάσωσιν, ’past, beyond’ (τάς γε παρὲξ ἐλάσωσιν ’drive past them’) · also prep. + acc.: ’past, beyond’ (παρὲξ τὴν νῆσον ἐλαύνετε ’drive past the island’) · also adv., ’aside, apart, besides’ (ἄλλα παρὲξ μεμνώμεθα ’let us remember other things apart from this’)
πατρίδ: πατρίς — fatherland, native land; fem. acc. sg., elided (πατρίδ’ = πατρίδα)
πατρίδα: πατρίς — native land, fatherland; fem. acc. sg. (φίλην ... πατρίδα γαῖαν ’his dear fatherland’)
πατρίδι: πατρίς — of one’s fathers, native; adj., fem. dat. sg., agreeing with γαίῃ: ’native (land)’
πεπνυμένος: πέπνυμαι — have one’s wits about one, be prudent; perf. part. masc. nom. sg. (trad. linked to πνέω ’breathe’, though uncertain), stock epithet: ’prudent’
περ: περ — even, though; concessive particle, esp. with a participle (= Attic καίπερ) · also used to intensify an adverb or pronoun rather than concede a point: ἔνθα περ ’in the very place where, just where’ · also after εἰ, ’if indeed, even if’: εἴ περ γάρ κεν ’if indeed ever’
περίφρων: περίφρων — circumspect, of sound understanding; fem. nom. sg., stock epithet of Penelope · also epithet of Arete: fem. nom. sg., ’the circumspect queen’
περὶ: περί — around, about; prep. + gen.: ’superior to, beyond’; also as adv.: ’exceedingly, surpassingly’ · also prep. + gen. in its plain sense ’about, concerning’ (περὶ πατρός ’about his father’) · also preverb in tmesis · + dat. · also + acc., of place, ’around, about’ (περὶ ἄστυ ’around the city’) · also + gen., of place, physically ’around, encircling’ (περὶ σπείους γλαφυροῖο ’around the hollow cave’), distinct from the comparative ’beyond’ sense above · also + dat. in the fixed idiom περὶ κῆρι ’exceedingly, at heart’ (περὶ κῆρι τιμήσουσιν ’will honor him at heart’) · also + dat., of place, ’around, about’ (περὶ χροῒ ’about the skin’) · also adverb of place, no case: ’round about’ (περὶ δ’ ἕρκος ἐλήλαται ’and round it a fence is driven’)
πηνελόπεια: Πηνελόπεια — Penelope, wife of Odysseus; nom. sg.
πικρόγαμοί: πικρόγαμος — of bitter marriage (πικρός ’bitter’ + γάμος); masc. nom. pl.
ποιήεντα: ποιήεις — grassy; adj., neut. acc. pl., epithet of ἄγκεα ’glens’
ποιμένα: ποιμήν — shepherd; masc. acc. sg. (ποιμένα λαῶν ’shepherd of the people’, apposition)
πολλά: πολύς — much, many; neut. nom. pl. (agreeing with ἔγχεα): ’many’ · also neut. acc. pl., object of a verb: ’many things’ (παλαιά τε πολλά τε εἰδώς ’knowing many old things’) · also neut. acc. pl., adjectival with a noun: ’many’ (πολλά τε δῶρα ’and many gifts’)
πολλὰ: πολύς — much, many; neut. acc. pl.: ’many things, greatly’ · also neut. nom. pl., plain attributive adj. agreeing with a neut. pl. noun (πολλὰ ... δάκρυα ’many tears’) · also neut. acc. pl., plain attributive adj. (κτήματα πολλὰ ’many possessions’) · also neut. acc. pl. used adverbially: ’again and again’ (πολλὰ περιτροπέοντες) · also neut. nom. pl. as substantive, subject: οἷά τε πολλὰ γίγνεται ’as many things happen’
πολύμητις: πολύμητις — of many wiles, epithet of Odysseus (built on μῆτις ’cunning intelligence’); masc. nom. sg.
ποτ: ποτέ — once, at some time, ever; enclitic adv., elided (ποτ’ = ποτέ)
ποτὶ: πρός — to, toward, against; prep., epic ποτί, here as preverb in tmesis (ποτὶ … βάλε = προσέβαλε) · also a plain preposition + acc., no tmesis: ποτὶ τοῖχον ’against the wall’ · also + dat. ‘against’ · also + dat., ’on, upon’: ποτὶ χθονί ’on the ground’
προσέειπε: προσεῖπον — speak to, address; aor. 3 sg., epic uncontracted (= Attic προσεῖπε)
προσέειπεν: προσεῖπον — speak to, address; aor. 3 sg., epic uncontracted, augment ἐ- kept (= Attic προσεῖπε)
προσέφη: πρόσφημι — speak to, address; aor. 3 sg.
πρὶν: πρίν — before, until; adv./conj., + inf. (grave, mid-clause form) · also τὸ πρίν, substantivized with the article: ‘formerly, at first’, no infinitive · also bare adv. ’formerly’, no art./inf. · also + aor. subj., ’before’ (πρὶν … ἐπέλθῃ ’before it comes upon’) · also + opt.: ’before’ (πρὶν τλαίη ’before he would bring himself’) · also adv. with a finite verb, ’before that, sooner’ (πρὶν … ἀγείρετο ’before that … came gathering’) · also + fut. indic.: ’before’ (πρὶν … γαῖα καθέξει ’before the earth covers’) · also with a bare noun, the verb understood: ’before’ (πρὶν ὥρη ’before it is time’)
πρὸς: πρός — towards, against, to; prep. + acc. · also a plain adverb, no case governed: ’besides, in addition’ · also + dat.: πρὸς ἀλλήλῃσιν ἔχονται ’cling close to one another’ · also + gen., ’from, under the protection of’ (πρὸς Διός εἰσιν ’are from Zeus’) · also + dat., ’against’ (ῥαίοιτο πρὸς οὔδεϊ ’be dashed against the floor’) · also + dat., ’in addition to’ (πρὸς τοῖσί τε ὕπνος ’and sleep in addition to these’) · also + gen., of direction: ’toward, on the side of’ (πρὸς Βορέαο ’toward the North Wind’) · also + gen., in an appeal: ’by (your father)’ (πρὸς πατρὸς γουνάζομαι) · also as preverb in tmesis: με πρὸς μῦθον ἔειπε = με προσέειπε μῦθον ’spoke a word to me’
πρῶτα: πρῶτος — first; neut. acc. pl. used adverbially: ’first’
πυκνὰ: πυκνός — thick, dense; neut. acc. pl. · also neut. acc. pl. used adverbially: ’thickly, closely’ (πυκνὰ ῥωγαλέην ’thickly ragged’)
πόλινδ: πόλις — city; fem. acc. sg. with -δε suffix, elided (πόλινδ’ = πόλινδε): ’to the city’
πόλινδε: πόλις — city; acc. sg. + suffix -δε ’towards’: ’to the city’
πόποι: πόποι — (in ὢ πόποι) exclamation of surprise or displeasure: ’ah! well!’; origin unknown
πότμον: πότμος — fate, doom, death; masc. acc. sg.
πύλον: Πύλος — Pylos, city in the Peloponnese, home of Nestor; acc. sg.
πᾶσαν: πᾶς — all, every; fem. acc. sg., agreeing with ἰθύν: ’for every (undertaking)’ · also ’the whole’ (of a single extent, not distributive ’every’): πᾶσαν ἠοίην ’the whole morning’, acc. of duration
σ: σύ — you (sg.); encl. acc. sg., elided (σ’ = σε): ’you’ · also σός — your, yours; neut. nom./acc. pl., elided (σ’ = σά): τὰ σ’ αὐτοῦ κήδε’ ’your own troubles’
σιάλους: σίαλος — fat hog, fattened pig; masc. acc. pl.
σκῆπτρον: σκῆπτρον — staff, sceptre (badge of the right to speak); neut. acc. sg.
σοι: σύ — you (sg.); encl. dat. sg.: ’to, for you’
σοῦ: σύ — you (sg.); gen. sg.: ’of you, your’
στήθεσσιν: στῆθος — breast, chest; neut. dat. pl., epic -εσσι(ν) (= Attic στήθεσι)
στρόφος: στρόφος — twisted cord, rope; masc. nom. sg.
συναντόμενος: συναντάομαι — meet, encounter; pres. part. mid. masc. nom. sg., epic (= Attic συναντώμενος)
σφιν: σφεῖς — they; epic encl. dat. pl./sg. pron.: ’to/for them’
σύας: σῦς (ὗς) — swine, pig; masc./fem. acc. pl.
σύνθεο: συντίθημι — put together; mid. take to heart, mark; aor. imper. mid. 2 sg., unaugmented, epic (= Attic σύνθου)
σὺ: σύ — you (sg.); nom. sg. (grave, mid-clause form)
σὺν: σύν — with, together with; prep. + dat. · also as adverb, ’together’, or as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb: σὺν … κάλυψε = συνεκάλυψε ’covered up’; σὺν … ἔπεσον = συνέπεσον ’fell together, clashed’ · also adverb ’along, with (us)’ construed with ἔχοντες, which takes the object (σὺν … χεῖρας ἔχοντες ’having hands along with us’)
τ: τε (elided τ’) — and; ’epic τε’ also marks a standing fact · after οὔ νυ perhaps τοι ’to you’ · also in a question, an expressive epic τε with no connective force, giving a note of doubt or wonder (πῶς τε ...; ’how, pray...?’) · also in ἦ τ’ (= ἦ τε), a strengthened affirmation: ’truly, surely’ (ἦ τ’ ἂν πολὺ κέρδιον ἦεν ’it would surely have been far better’) · also after a relative of size or amount, with no connective force: ὅσην τ’ ὄρεος κορυφήν ’as large as a mountain’s peak’ · also after ἤ ’than’, with no connective force: ἤ τ’ οἰωνοί ’than birds’
τά: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); neut. nom./acc. pl.; also relative: ’which’ (accented τά before a following enclitic) · also article-like with ἄλλα, ’the other (things)’ (τά περ ἄλλα ’in the other matters’)
τάδε: ὅδε — this, this here; demonstrative pron., neut. nom./acc. pl.: ’these things’
τέρποντο: τέρπομαι — take pleasure, enjoy oneself; impf. 3 pl.
τέτυκται: τεύχω — make, build; pass. come to pass, happen; perf. pass. 3 sg.: ’has been made, has come to pass’
τίς: τίς, τί — who? what?; interrog. pron., masc. nom. sg. · also the enclitic indefinite τις accented before a following enclitic, not interrogative: ’someone, anyone’ (ἤν τίς τοι εἴπῃσι ’if someone tells you’)
ταλασίφρονος: ταλασίφρων — enduring-minded, steadfast; gen. sg. (epithet of Odysseus, from τλῆναι ’endure’)
ταῦτα: οὗτος, αὕτη, τοῦτο — this; neut. nom./acc. pl.: ’these things’
τε: τε — and, both...and; enclitic connective; also ’epic τε’ marking a standing general truth in relative clauses
τελευτήσας: τελευτάω — bring to an end, complete, finish; aor. part. masc. nom. sg.: ’having finished’
τετελεσμένον: τελέω — bring to pass, fulfil; perf. pass. part. neut. nom. sg., periphrastic with ἔσται: ’shall stand fulfilled’ · also periphrastic with the pres. ἐστίν rather than fut. ἔσται, of a thing already fixed by fate: ’it is a thing ordained, it is decreed’ · also periphrastic with the opt. εἴη, in a wish: ’may it be fulfilled’ (τετελεσμένον εἴη)
τευ: τις, τι — someone, something; indefinite pron., masc./fem. gen. sg., epic τευ (= Attic τινός)
τηλέμαχ: Τηλέμαχος — Telemachus, son of Odysseus; masc. voc. sg., elided (Τηλέμαχ’ = Τηλέμαχε)
τηλέμαχος: Τηλέμαχος — Telemachus, son of Odysseus; nom. sg.
τηλεμάχῳ: Τηλέμαχος — Telemachus, son of Odysseus; masc. dat. sg.
τι: τις, τι — someone, something; neut. acc. sg., used adverbially with negatives ’at all’ · also adjectival indefinite: ’some, any’ (τι δήμιον ἄλλο ’some other public matter’) · also adverbial without a negative: ’in some way, in some measure’ (τι κατὰ πρῆξιν ’on some business’) · also as a substantive object, in a question: ’anything, something’ (ἦ ῥά τι ἴδμεν ’do we know anything’) · also the neut. of τις forming, with a preceding ὅ, the indefinite relative ὅ τι ’whatever, that which’ (αὔδα ὅ τι φρονέεις ’say whatever you have in mind’) · also ὅ τι as an adverbial acc. in an indirect question: ’why’ · also as a substantive object in a statement: ’something’ (καί τι ἴσασι ’they know something’)
τοί: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. nom. pl. ’they’ · also relative: ’who’ · also encl. dat. sg. pron. σύ ’to you’ (= τοι, accented before a following enclitic, e.g. τοί τι) · also τοι, the affirming particle, accented τοί before an enclitic: ἀλλ’ ἦ τοί σε ’but truly you’
τοι: σύ — you (sg.); encl. dat. sg.: ’to/for you’ · also τοι, the affirming particle: ’you know, indeed’ (esp. in ἦ τοι, οὔ τοι); the two are not always easy to keep apart
τοιαῦτα: τοιοῦτος — such, of such a kind; demonstr. pron./adj., neut. nom./acc. pl.: ’such things’
τοιγὰρ: τοιγάρ — well then, accordingly; particle introducing a response to a request
τοὶ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. nom. pl.: ’they’; also relative: ’who’ · also τοι, the affirming particle (ἀλλ’ ἦ τοι ’but truly’), as the grave-accented form τοὶ
τοῖον: τοῖος — such, of such a kind; neut. acc. sg. used adverbially: ’in such a way’ · also masc. acc. sg., agreeing with a noun or pronoun: ’such a one as’ (σέ γε τοῖον ἐγείνατο ’bore a son such as you’) · also ’so’, qualifying an adj. · also neut. nom./acc. sg., agreeing with a neut. noun: τοῖον … ἔρνος (acc.), τοῖον … δόρυ (nom.) ’such a shoot, such a trunk’
τοῖος: τοῖος — such, of such a kind; masc. nom. sg. (τοῖος ... οἷον ’such as’)
τοῖσι: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. dat. pl. ’to/among them’
τοῖσιν: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. dat. pl. ’from/to them’
τοῦτο: οὗτος, αὕτη, τοῦτο — this; neut. nom./acc. sg.
τρῶές: Τρώς — Trojan; masc. nom. pl. Τρῶες, accented before the enclitic τε
τυκτῷ: τυκτός — wrought, made, fashioned (from τεύχω); adj., neut. dat. sg. (τυκτῷ δαπέδῳ ’the wrought, levelled floor’)
τόδε: ὅδε — this, this here; demonstrative pron., neut. nom./acc. sg.
τότε: τότε — then, at that time; adv.
τὰ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); neut. nom./acc. pl.: ’these things’ · also in the adverbial idiom τὰ πρῶτα, ’at first, first’ (not ’these things’) · also with a noun, pointing to it: ’those, the’ (τὰ σὰ γούνατα ’those knees of yours’) · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅ: which; neut. nom. pl. (μῆλα, τὰ … κατάκειτ’ ’the flocks, which lie’) · also relative, neut. acc. pl.: ’which’, object of the verb in its clause (ῥωγαλέα, τὰ … ὅρηαι ’torn, which you see’)
τὴν: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); fem. acc. sg. ’her’ · also ’it’, of a thing (τὴν = the clothing): fem. acc. sg. · also with a noun, article-like: τὴν ὁδόν ’that journey’ · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅ: whom; fem. acc. sg. (τὴν Ὠκεανὸς τέκε ’whom Oceanus begot’) · also ’the other’, contrasted with a preceding τὴν … μέν: fem. acc. sg. (τὴν δέ ’the other one’) · also article-like with a numeral: ’the one’ (τὴν μὲν ἴαν ’the one portion’)
τὸ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); neut. nom./acc. sg. (τὸ πάροιθεν ’that which was before’) · also with a noun, pointing to it: ’that, the’ (τὸ σῆμα ’that mark’) · also article-like before the adverb πάρος: ’as before’ (ὡς τὸ πάρος περ) · also article-like before an ordinal, adverbial: τὸ τρίτον ’the third time’ · also distributive, neut. nom./acc. sg.: τὸ μὲν … τὸ δὲ ’one thing … another’ · also article-like before the adverb πρόσθεν: ’formerly’ (τὸ πρόσθεν ὄλοντο ’died long before’) · also article-like before a substantivized adjective, neut.: τὸ μέλαν ’the dark (part)’
τὸν: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. acc. sg. ’him’ · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅ: whom, which; masc. acc. sg. (τὸν Ἀλφειὸς τέκε ’whom Alpheus begot’) · also demonstrative adjective with a noun: ’that, the’ (τὸν μῦθον ’that story, message’) · also demonstrative, distributive: masc. acc. sg. ’the one … the other’ (τὸν μὲν … τὸν δ’) · also article-like with a participle: τὸν ἐόντα ’me, the one who am’ · also article-like with a superlative or ordinal: ’the best’ (τὸν ἄριστον), ’the fourth’ (τὸν τέταρτον)
τὼ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun); masc. nom. dual: ’the two of them’  ·  also acc. dual, object of a verb of address: τὼ … προσέφη ’spoke to the two of them’ · also relative, nom. dual, ’who (the two)’: τοκῆε δύω, τὼ μὴ γείνασθαι ὄφελλον · also nom. dual with a noun, article-like: ’the two’ (τὼ … θεράποντε)
τῇ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); fem. dat. sg.: ’her, with her’ · also adverbial, ’there, in that place’, pointing back to a place just named (τῇ τόν γε μένον λοχόωντες ’there they lay in wait for him’) · also relative, fem. dat. sg., serving as an instrumental, ’with which’ (ῥάβδον, τῇ τ’ ἀνδρῶν ὄμματα θέλγει ’a wand, with which he charms men’s eyes’), not the personal pronoun · also relative adv., ’where, in the place where’ (τῇ δή μοι ἐείσατο χῶρος ἄριστος) · also adverbial, ’in that (event)’, pointing back to a contest just named: τῇ δ’ αὖτ’ Εὐρύαλος ἀπεκαίνυτο ’in that Euryalus in turn outdid all’ · also relative adv. of manner, with περ: ’in just the way that’ · also adv. of direction, ’thither, that way’ · also with a noun, article-like: fem. dat. sg. ’the’ (τῇ δεκάτῃ ’on the tenth’)
τῶν: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); gen. pl. ’of these things, of them’ · also with a noun, article-like: τῶν ἄλλων ἀνέμων ’of the other winds’ · also distributive, ’of the one … of the other’ (τῶν μὲν … τῶν δ’ ’of the one band … of the other’) · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅ: gen. pl. ’of whom, whose’ (τῶν ὕβρις τε βίη τε … ἵκει ’whose insolence and violence reach’)
τῷ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc./neut. dat. sg.; also relative: ’in which’ · the relative dat. sg. also serves as an instrumental, ’with which’ (τῷ δάμνησι ’with which she overpowers’) · also adverbial ’therefore, and so’ (τῷ οὔ τινα οἶδα ’so I know no one’) · also article-like with a noun: ’that, the same’ (ἤματι τῷ αὐτῷ ’on that same day’) · also demonstrative instrumental, of a thing just named: ’with it’ (τῷ ἀπὸ πείσματ’ ἔκοψα ’with it I cut the cables off’) · also demonstrative of a thing just named, before a preposition: ’it’ (τῷ δ’ ἐν ’and on it’, τῷ δ’ ὑπό ’and beneath it’)
υἱάσι: υἱός — son; masc. dat. pl., epic stem υἱ- (= Attic υἱοῖς/υἱέσι)
φάτο: φημί — say, speak; impf. 3 sg. mid., unaugmented (= ἔφατο)
φίλην: φίλος — dear, one’s own; fem. acc. sg.
φιλομηλεΐδῃ: Φιλομηλεΐδης — Philomeleides, a legendary king of Lesbos known only from this wrestling-story; masc. dat. sg.
φιλότητά: φιλότης — friendship, affection; fem. acc. sg.
φρέν: φρήν — mind, heart, wits; fem. acc. sg., elided (φρέν’ = φρένα), accusative of respect: ’in heart’
φρονέω: φρονέω — think, have understanding, be minded; pres. 1 sg.: ’I understand’
φυτεύει: φυτεύω — plant, beget; pres. 3 sg., fig. ’set in motion (a disaster)’
φῆ: φημί — say, declare, assert; impf. 3 sg., unaugmented (= ἔφη): ’said, declared’
χλαίνας: χλαῖνα — a thick cloak, mantle; fem. acc. pl.
χροῒ: χρώς — skin, flesh, the body’s surface; dat. sg. χροΐ
ἀέθλοις: ἄεθλος — contest, trial, labor (Attic ἆθλος); masc. dat. pl., epic (= Attic ἄθλοις)
ἀγήνορας: ἀγήνωρ — very manly, overbearing, lordly (rendered ’lordly’ throughout); masc. acc. pl.
ἀγαθὸς: ἀγαθός — good, brave, noble; adj., masc. nom. sg.
ἀγρῶν: ἀγρός — field, countryside; masc. gen. pl.
ἀγόρευον: ἀγορεύω — speak, say, declare; impf. 3 pl.
ἀεικέα: ἀεικής — unseemly, shameful, unfitting; masc. acc. sg. · also neut. acc. pl., used substantivally: ’unseemly things’ (ἀεικέα μερμηρίζων ’pondering unseemly things’) · also fem. acc. sg., agreeing with πήρην: ’unseemly, shabby (wallet)’ · also neut. acc. pl., attributive: ’shameful (deeds)’ (ἀεικέα ἔργ’)
ἀθάνατοι: ἀθάνατος — immortal, deathless; masc. nom. pl.: ’the immortals’
ἀθηναίη: Ἀθηναίη — Athena; fem. nom. sg., epic full form (= Ἀθήνη)
ἀληθείην: ἀλήθεια — truth; fem. acc. sg. (Ionic ἀληθείη)
ἀλλήλους: ἀλλήλων — one another; reciprocal pron., masc. acc. pl.
ἀμειβόμενος: ἀμείβομαι — answer, reply; pres. part. masc. nom. sg. mid.
ἀμφ: ἀμφί (elided ἀμφ’) — around, about, concerning; + dat. · also + acc., ’around, with, accompanying’ (ἀμφ’ Ὀδυσῆα ’with, around Odysseus’) · also + gen., ’about, concerning’ (ἀμφ’ Ἄρεος φιλότητος ’about the love of Ares’) · also with ὀστεόφιν, ’around’ (ἀμφ’ ὀστεόφιν θὶς ’a heap around the bones’)
ἀμφοτέροισι: ἀμφότερος — both (of two); masc. dat. pl., epic -οισι (= Attic -οις)
ἀμύμονος: ἀμύμων — blameless, excellent (an old epithet whose exact force is uncertain); gen. sg.
ἀνάγκῃ: ἀνάγκη — necessity, compulsion; dat. sg., dat. of manner: ’under compulsion’
ἀνάκτων: ἄναξ — lord, master; masc. gen. pl. (θεῶν ἀνάκτων ’of the lord gods’)
ἀνάλκιδες: ἄναλκις — without might, strengthless, feeble (ἀ- + ἀλκή); adj., masc. nom. pl., predicate
ἀναστάς: ἀνίστημι — raise up; intrans. aor. part. act. masc. nom. sg. ἀναστάς: ’having risen up, rising’
ἀνστάντες: ἀνίστημι — stand up, rise; intrans. aor. part. masc. nom. pl., epic apocope (ἀνστάντες = ἀναστάντες)
ἀντίον: ἀντίον — face to face, in answer, opposite; adv.
ἀορτήρ: ἀορτήρ — strap, sling (by which a bag hangs); masc. nom. sg.
ἀπαμειβόμενος: ἀπαμείβομαι — answer, reply; pres. part. nom. sg. masc.
ἀργεῖοι: Ἀργεῖοι — the Argives, i.e. the Greeks; masc. nom. pl.
ἀτρεΐδην: Ἀτρεΐδης — son of Atreus (patronymic, here of Agamemnon); masc. acc. sg.  ·  also used of Menelaus: Ἀτρεΐδην Μενέλαον ’Menelaus, son of Atreus’
ἀτρεΐδης: Ἀτρεΐδης — son of Atreus (patronymic); masc. nom. sg.
ἀτρεκέως: ἀτρεκής — exact, unswerving; adv. ἀτρεκέως: ’exactly, precisely’
ἀτὰρ: ἀτάρ — but, and; epic conj. (by-form of αὐτάρ)
ἀφικάνω: ἀφικάνω — arrive at, come to; pres. 1 sg., epic by-form of ἀφικνέομαι: ’I have come to’
ἀχαιοί: Ἀχαιοί — the Achaeans, the Greeks; masc. nom. pl.
ἂν: ἄν — modal particle marking contingency (with subj. = future contingency, with opt. = potential) · also with a secondary indicative (impf./aor.) marking an unreal, contrary-to-fact conclusion: ’would’ (οὐκ ἂν ... ἀγόρευες ’you would not be speaking’) · also = ἀνά (preposition/preverb ’up’) in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἂν … βαῖνε = ἀνέβαινε, ἂν … βάντες = ἀναβάντες) · also = ἀνά as a preposition + acc.: ’up through, up among’ (ἂν δόνακας ’up through the reeds’) · also in ὡς ἄν + opt., a purpose clause: ’so that … might’ (ὡς ἂν … ἑλοίμεθα ’so that we might seize’)
ἂρ: ἄρα — then, so, as it seems; inferential particle, grave form ἂρ (ἐπεὶ ἂρ δή ’since, as it seems’)
ἄγε: ἄγε — come now!; interjectional imper. of ἄγω, 2 sg. · also ἄγω — lead; impf. 3 sg., unaugmented (= ἦγε): ’led’ · also ἄγω — lead; pres. imper. 2 sg.: ’lead’ (μή μ’ ἄγε κεῖσ’ ’do not lead me there’)
ἄγκεα: ἄγκος — glen, valley, mountain-hollow; neut. acc. pl.
ἄκουσας: ἀκούω — hear; aor. 2 sg., unaugmented (= ἤκουσας), + gen. of source
ἄλγε: ἄλγος — pain, grief; neut. nom./acc. pl. (ἄλγεα, elided ἄλγε’)
ἄλλα: ἄλλος — other, another; neut. nom./acc. pl.
ἄλλοθεν: ἄλλοθεν — from elsewhere, from another place; adv. (ἄλλος + -θεν ’from’)
ἄν: ἄν — modal particle marking contingency (with subj. = future contingency, with opt. = potential)
ἄνακτα: ἄναξ — lord, king, master; masc. acc. sg.
ἄναξ: ἄναξ — lord, master; masc. nom. sg. · also voc. sg. (same form), in address: ’lord!’ (κλῦθι, ἄναξ ’hear me, lord’)
ἄρα: ἄρα — so, as it turned out, then; inferential particle
ἅ: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — who, which; relative pron., neut. nom./acc. pl.: ’what things’
ἅλιος: ἅλιος — of the sea, belonging to the sea; adj., masc. nom. sg., part of the standing epithet γέρων ἅλιος νημερτής ’the old man of the sea’ (of Proteus)
ἅμ: ἅμα (elided ἅμ’) — together with, at the same time as; adv./prep. + dat.
ἐγώ: ἐγώ — I; nom. sg. (accented ἐγώ before the enclitic τοι that follows) · also accented ἐγώ before the enclitic μιν that follows · also accented before the enclitic τε: σύ τ’ ἐγώ τε ’you and I’
ἐγὼν: ἐγώ — I; nom. sg., form used before a vowel
ἐλθόντα: ἔρχομαι — go, come; aor. part. masc. acc. sg.: ’having come, on his coming’
ἐμεῖο: ἐγώ — I; epic gen. sg. ἐμεῖο (= Attic ἐμοῦ)
ἐμεῦ: ἐγώ — I; gen. sg., epic (= Attic ἐμοῦ): ’from me’ · also gen. as object of a verb of remembering: μνήσῃ ἐμεῦ ’you may remember me’ · also gen. with ἀέκητι: ’(against) my (will)’ (ἐμεῦ ἀέκητι)
ἐμοῖσι: ἐμός — my, mine; masc./neut. dat. pl., epic -οισι (= Attic ἐμοῖς)
ἐμός: ἐμός — my, mine; masc. nom. sg.
ἐν: ἐν — in, on, among; + dat.; also used as an adverb, ’in it, there’ · also as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἐν … βάλῃ = ἐμβάλῃ ’cast in’; ἐν … χεῦον = ἔγχεον ’pour in’)
ἐναλίγκιον: ἐναλίγκιος — like, resembling (+ dat.); masc. acc. sg., agreeing with the speaker: ’like (a beggar)’
ἐντυνόμενοι: ἐντύνω — make ready, prepare; pres. part. mid. masc. nom. pl.
ἐνὶ: ἐν (epic ἐνί) — in, on, among; + dat. · also adverb or preverb, no case: ’therein’ (ἔνθ’ ἐνὶ πέπλοι ... βεβλήατο ’therein coverlets were laid’) · also + gen., of a person’s house: ’in the house of’ (ἐνὶ Κίρκης ’in Circe’s house’)
ἐξ: ἐκ (ἐξ before a vowel) — out of, from; + gen. · also as a preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἐξ … ἕντο = ἐξέντο, from ἐξίημι ’send out, put away (desire)’)
ἐξερέῃσι: ἐξερέομαι — search out, range over, explore; pres. subj. 3 sg., epic -ῃσι, generalizing with ὁπότε (no ἄν/κε needed): ’ranges over’
ἐπ: ἐπί (elided ἐπ’) — on, upon, over, towards, against; + dat./acc./gen. · also as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἐπ’ … χεῦε = ἐπέχευε ‘poured upon’) · also + dat., of time: ’in, within’ (ἐπ’ ἤματι ’in a day’)
ἐπάλαισεν: παλαίω — wrestle; aor. 3 sg., + dat. of the opponent: ’he wrestled (against)’
ἐπέτελλεν: ἐπιτέλλω — command, charge, enjoin; impf. 3 sg.: ‘gave command’
ἐπήλυθε: ἐπέρχομαι — come upon; aor. 3 sg., epic ἐπήλυθε (= Attic ἐπῆλθε)
ἐπήρετμοι: ἐπήρετμος — at the oar, seated ready to row; masc. nom. pl. · also of ships, ’fitted/equipped with oars’: νῆες ἐπήρετμοι ’oared ships’ (masc. nom. pl.)
ἐπικεύσω: ἐπικεύθω — hide further, keep back, conceal in addition; fut. 1 sg.
ἐπιχθονίων: ἐπιχθόνιος — upon the earth (epithet of mortals, as against the gods); masc./fem. gen. pl.
ἐπὶ: ἐπί — on, upon, over, towards, against; + dat./acc./gen. · also as adverb, no case expressed: ’to it, over it; besides’ (θεοὶ δ’ ἐπὶ μάρτυροι ’witnesses to it’; ἐπὶ κτέρεα κτερεΐξαι ’besides’) · also + dat., ’beyond, over and above, more than’ (ἐπὶ γαστέρι κύντερον ’more shameless than the belly’) · also adverb of sequence, ’next, thereupon’ (ἦλθε δ’ ἐπὶ ψυχή ’and next came the soul’) · also as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb: ἐπὶ … τέταλτο = ἐπιτέταλτο ’was laid upon, entrusted’ · also + acc. of time: ’for, over’ (ἐπὶ χρόνον ’for a time’) · also + dat., ’in charge of, over’ (ἐπὶ κτεάτεσσιν ’over my possessions’)
ἐς: εἰς (epic ἐς) — into, to; + acc. · also as a preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb with no case expressed (ἐς … ἦλθον = εἰσῆλθον ’came in’)
ἐστίν: εἰμί — be; pres. 3 sg., ν-movable form
ἐφήσει: ἐφίημι — send/let loose upon, launch at; fut. 3 sg.
ἐφίλει: φιλέω — love, treat kindly; impf. 3 sg., augmented: ’was fond of, cherished’
ἐφῆκεν: ἐφίημι — send/let loose upon; aor. 3 sg., augmented
ἐόντες: εἰμί — be; pres. part. masc. nom. pl., epic (= Attic ὄντες): ’being’
ἐὼν: εἰμί — be; pres. part. masc. nom. sg., epic (= Attic ὤν)
ἑλένην: Ἑλένη — Helen, wife of Menelaus; fem. acc. sg.
ἑλέσθαι: αἱρέω — take, take up; aor. mid. inf.: ’to take (for oneself)’
ἑταῖροι: ἑταῖρος — companion, comrade; masc. nom. pl. · also voc. pl. (same form), address: ’companions!’
ἑὴν: ἑός (= ὅς, ἥ, ὅν possessive) — his own, her own; 3rd-person reflexive possessive adj., fem. acc. sg. ἑήν, agreeing with εὐνήν: ’his own (lair)’ · also agreeing with πατρίδα: ’his own’ (ἑὴν ἐς πατρίδα γαῖαν ’to his own fatherland’)
ἑὸν: ἑός — his own, her own (possessive, by-form of ὅς); masc. acc. sg. · also neut. acc./nom. sg., agreeing with a neuter noun (δῶμα ἑὸν ’his own hall’)
ἔβαλε: βάλλω — throw, cast, throw down; aor. 3 sg., here in tmesis with κατά (κὰδ δ’ ἔβαλε = κατέβαλε): ’threw down’
ἔβαν: βαίνω — go, walk; aor. 3 pl., epic (= Attic ἔβησαν)
ἔειπε: εἶπον — say, speak, tell; aor. 3 sg., epic uncontracted, augment ἐ- kept before the root’s own ει- (= Attic εἶπε)
ἔην: εἰμί — be; impf. 3 sg., epic (= Attic ἦν)
ἔλαφος: ἔλαφος — deer, hind; fem. nom. sg.
ἔμμεναι: εἰμί — be; pres. inf., epic (= Attic εἶναι)
ἔνθ: ἔνθα (elided ἔνθ’) — there, then; adverb of place or time
ἔπεσσιν: ἔπος — word; neut. dat. pl., epic -εσσι(ν) (= Attic -εσι)
ἔπος: ἔπος — word, speech, thing said; neut. nom./acc. sg.
ἔργα: ἔργον — deed, work; neut. nom./acc. pl.
ἔριδος: ἔρις — strife, quarrel, contention; fem. gen. sg.
ἔς: εἰς (epic ἐς) — into, to; prep. + acc.
ἔστιν: εἰμί — be; pres. 3 sg., impersonal: ’it is possible’ · also plain copula, personal: ’is’ (ἀργύρεος ... ἔστιν ἅπας ’it is entirely silver’) · also with a dat. of the possessor, ’have’ (ἅσσα μοι ἔστιν ’whatever I have’) · also existential, ’there is’ (ἐν … νηὶ … βρῶσίς τε πόσις τε ἔστιν ’in the ship there is food and drink’)
ἔτλης: τλάω — endure, dare, bring oneself to; aor. 2 sg., root aorist: ’you dared’
ἔφαθ: φημί — say, speak; impf. 3 sg. mid. (ἔφατο, elided ἔφαθ’, τ>θ before rough breathing)
ἔφασκεν: φάσκω — say, assert; impf. 3 sg., iterative: ’she kept saying’
ἔφατ: φημί — say, speak; impf. 3 sg. mid., augmented, elided (ἔφατ’ = ἔφατο)
ἔχοντα: ἔχω — have, hold; pres. part. masc. acc. sg.: ‘holding’ · also with ἄλγεα, masc. acc. sg.: ’suffering, enduring’ (κρατέρ’ ἄλγε’ ἔχοντα ’beset by harsh pains’)
ἔχοντες: ἔχω — have, hold; pres. part. masc. nom. pl.
ἡγεμόνευε: ἡγεμονεύω — lead the way, be the guide (+ dat.); impf. 3 sg. (augment not visible on ἡ-) · also pres. imper. 2 sg.: ’lead the way!’
ἢ: ἤ — or; disjunctive conj. (epic ἠέ/ἤ) · also ’than’ after a comparative: κρεῖσσον … ἢ ὅτε ’better than when’ · also ’before’ after a verb of anticipating (ἔφθης … ἢ ἐγώ ’you got here before I did’) · also introducing the first alternative of an indirect question: ’whether’ (ἢ ἔτι … ἦέ τις ’whether still … or someone’) · also ’than’ after a verb of preferring: βουλοίμην … ἢ … ἀνάσσειν ’I would rather … than rule’
ἣν: ὅς, ἥ, ὅν (possessive) — his own, her own; fem. acc. sg. · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅν: whom, which (fem. acc. sg.)
ἤγαγον: ἄγω — lead, bring; aor. 3 pl., reduplicated · also aor. 1 sg. (the same ending serves both persons): ’I brought’ (ἤγαγον ἐκ Σκύρου ’I brought him from Scyros’)
ἤδη: ἤδη — now, already, at once; adv.
ἤθελον: ἐθέλω — be willing, wish; impf. 3 pl., augmented: ’they wished’
ἥ: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — who, which; relative pron., fem. nom. sg. · also ὁ, ἡ, τό (personal/demonstrative pronoun): she; fem. nom. sg. (ἥ γε ’she indeed’, of the ship)
ἥμενος: ἧμαι — sit; pres. part. masc. nom. sg.: ’sitting’
ἥνδανε: ἁνδάνω — please, be pleasing to; impf. 3 sg., augmented (η- from the root’s original digamma, contracted; the same augment as the uncontracted ἑήνδανε in this part; unaugmented ἄνδανε); + dat.: ’was pleasing to’
ἦ: ἦ — truly, verily; affirming particle · also interrogative particle introducing an earnest question · also = ἤ ’or’, in the correlative ἠέ … ἦ ’whether … or’ · also ἠμί — say, speak; unaugmented aor./impf. 3 sg. (= ἔφη), closing or introducing direct speech: ’he/she said’ (ἦ ῥα ’so he said’) · also ’or’, the second alternative of a pair of questions with no preceding ἠέ: ζώει … ἦ τέθνηκε ’alive or dead’; ἢ ἔτ’ ἔχει … ἦ μιν ἀτιμάζουσιν ’whether … or’
ἦγεν: ἄγω — lead, bring; impf. 3 sg., ν-movable: ’brought, was leading’
ἦεν: εἰμί — be; impf. 3 sg., epic (= Attic ἦν)
ἦμαρ: ἦμαρ — day (epic for ἡμέρα); neut. nom./acc. sg.
ἦρχε: ἄρχω — begin, rule; impf. 3 sg., + gen. ’began (the speaking)’ · also ’go first, lead the way’ (no gen.): ἦρχε δ’ Ἀθήνη ’and Athena went first, led the way’ · also + gen. of the way: ἦρχε ὁδοῖο ’led the way’ · also absolute: ’ruled, was king’
ἧς: ὅς, ἥ, ὅν (possessive) — his own, her own; fem. gen. sg. · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅν: whose, of whom/which (fem. gen. sg.)
ἰδέειν: ὁράω (aor. stem εἰδ-) — see; aor. inf., epic uncontracted (= Attic ἰδεῖν)
ἰότητι: ἰότης — will, wish, favour; fem. dat. sg.: ’by the will of’
ἱέντες: ἵημι — throw, hurl, let fly; pres. part. masc. nom. pl.: ’throwing’
ἱκέσθαι: ἱκνέομαι — come to, reach, arrive at; aor. inf.
ἱκόμην: ἱκνέομαι — come, arrive; aor. mid. 1 sg., unaugmented: ’I came’
ἱστίη: ἱστίη — hearth, hearth-fire, household; fem. nom. sg., Ionic (= Attic ἑστία)
ἴδον: ὁράω — see; aor. 1 sg., unaugmented, from the root of εἶδον (= εἶδον) · also aor. 3 pl. (the same ending serves both persons): ’they saw’
ἴλιον: Ἴλιος — Ilios, Troy; fem. acc. sg.
ἴομεν: εἶμι — go; pres. subj. 1 pl. (hortatory): ’let us go’ · also subj. in a temporal clause with ἄν/κε: ’we go, are going’ (ὄφρ’ ἂν … ἀγροὺς ἴομεν ’while we go through the fields’)
ἴστω: οἶδα — know; perf. imper. 3 sg.: ’let it/him/her know’ (calling something to witness)
ἴσχει: ἴσχω — hold, hold back, restrain (intensive of ἔχω); pres. 3 sg.
ἵκοντο: ἱκνέομαι — come, arrive at, reach; aor. 3 pl.; with short ι (by metre) unaugmented; where the metre makes the ι long, augmented (the spelling cannot show it)
ἵν: ἵνα — so that, in order that; conj., elided (ἵν’ = ἵνα) · also relative adverb of place, ’where’ (= Attic οὗ): τῶν ἐνὶ δήμῳ, ἵν’ οἴχεται ’among those of the land where he has gone’
ἵπποισι: ἵππος — horse; masc. dat. pl., epic -οισι (= Attic -οις)
ὀδυσεύς: Ὀδυσσεύς — Odysseus; nom. sg., single-σ metrical variant
ὀδυσεὺς: Ὀδυσσεύς — Odysseus; masc. nom. sg., single-σ metrical variant Ὀδυσεύς
ὀδυσσεύς: Ὀδυσσεύς — Odysseus, the poem’s hero; nom. sg.
ὀδυσσεὺς: Ὀδυσσεύς — Odysseus, the poem’s hero; nom. sg.
ὀδυσσῆος: Ὀδυσσεύς — Odysseus; gen. sg. (double-σ, metrical variant of single-σ Ὀδυσῆος)
ὀδυσῆος: Ὀδυσσεύς — Odysseus; gen. sg. (single-σ metrical variant of Ὀδυσσῆος)
ὀπίσσω: ὀπίσσω — behind; in Homer also ’hereafter, in time to come’; adv. · also ’back, home again’, of return (οἴκαδ’ ὀπίσσω ’back home’)
ὁ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. nom. sg. · also article-like with an adjective and a name: ’the’ (ὁ θρασὺς Ὀδυσσεύς ’bold Odysseus’) · also article-like with a noun: ’the’ (ὁ γέρων ’the old man’) · also distributive, masc. nom. sg.: ’the one’ (ὁ μὲν οὐρανὸν εὐρὺν ἱκάνει ’the one reaches the broad heaven’)
ὁμιλήσειεν: ὁμιλέω — be in company with, meet, consort with; aor. opt. 3 sg., wish: ’might he come among’
ὁπότ: ὁπότε (elided ὁπότ’) — when, whenever; temporal conj., here introducing a vivid simile · also with the optative, iterative in past time: ’whenever’ (ὁπότ’ ἰθύσει’ … ’whenever he made a dash’)
ὃς: ὅς, ἥ, ὅν (relative) — who, which; masc. nom. sg. · also possessive ὅς, ἥ, ὅν: his own, her own (masc. nom. sg.) · also plain demonstrative, ’he’ (ὃς γὰρ δεύτατος ἦλθεν), not a relative
ὄπισθε: ὄπισθε(ν) — behind, from behind; adv. · also ’hereafter, afterwards’ (of time)
ὄρινε: ὀρίνω — stir up, rouse; pres. imper. 2 sg., after μηδέ in a prohibition: ’do not stir up’
ὄρχαμος: ὄρχαμος — chief, leader; masc. nom. sg. (ὄρχαμος ἀνδρῶν ’chief of men’)
ὅ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); neut. nom./acc. sg.; with γε: ’he’ · also relative, masc. nom. sg., accented before an enclitic: ’who’ (ὅ κε ... ἐφείη) · also = ὅτι ’that’; εἰς ὅ ’until’ · also relative, neut. nom./acc. sg.: ’which’ (ὅ οἱ πέρι δῶκεν Ἀθήνη ’which Athena gave her beyond others’) · also masc. nom. sg. pronoun ’he’ without γε, accented before an enclitic (ὅ σφιν ’he … to them’)
ὅθι: ὅθι — where; epic relative adverb (= Attic οὗ)
ὅτε: ὅτε — when; temporal conjunction · also ’since, now that’ (ὅτε πρότερός γε πύθοιτο ’since he learned of it first’) · also with the optative, hypothetical/conditional: ’if ever, whenever’ (ὅτε ... ἵκοι ’if ever such need should come upon me’) · also with the subjunctive, general: ’whenever’ (ὅτε στείχῃσ’ ἀνὰ ἄστυ ’whenever she goes through the town’) · also with the optative, iterative in past time: ’whenever’ (ὅτε μέλλοι ’whenever he was about to’) · also with the pres. indic., ’whereas, when’ (ὅτε τ’ ἄλλοι ἅπαξ θνῄσκουσ’ ἄνθρωποι ’whereas other men die only once’) · also in ὅτε μή, ’unless, except when’ (ὅτε μὴ θεὸς … θείη ’unless a god should make’)
ὑφορβός: ὑφορβός — swineherd (ὑπό + φέρβω ’feed’); masc. nom. sg.
ὑψηλοῖσι: ὑψηλός — high, lofty; adj., masc. dat. pl., epic -οισι (= Attic -οῖς)
ὕβριν: ὕβρις — insolence, wanton violence; fem. acc. sg.
ὠκύμοροί: ὠκύμορος — swift-doomed, early-doomed (ὠκύς + μόρος); masc. nom. pl.
ὡς: ὡς — as, how, that, when; with the optative introduces a wish: ’so may…’ (unaccented; accented ὥς / ὣς is ’thus’) · also ὡς + unaugmented ὄφελον + inf., an unfulfillable wish: ’would that...’ · also ὡς + opt., a purpose clause (= ἵνα): ’so that’ (ὡς τὸν χόλον ἐξακέσαιτο ’so that he might appease the anger’) · also exclamatory ὡς + adj. + inf.: ’how (good, etc.) it is to...’ (ὡς ἀγαθὸν ... λιπέσθαι ’how good a thing it is to be left behind’) · also plain ὡς + indic., ’as’ (ὡς σὺ κελεύεις ’as you command’) or ’how’ in an indirect question (ὡς ἐπὶ πόντον ἐλεύσομαι ’how I shall come upon the sea’) · also ὡς ἄν + subj., a purpose clause: ’so that’ (ὡς ἂν μὴ κλαίουσα κατὰ χρόα καλὸν ἰάπτῃς ’so that you might not mar your fair skin with weeping’) · also ὡς δ’ ὅτε introducing an epic simile, ’as when’, its clause taking indic. or ἄν/κε + subj. for a general case: ὡς δ’ ὅτ’ ἂν ... φανήῃ ’as when ... should appear’ · also comparative ’like’, placed after the noun it compares (ἀνέμου ὡς πνοιή ’like a blast of wind’) · also ὡς εἰ ’as if, like’ (ὡς εἰ πτερὸν ἠὲ νόημα ’as if a wing or a thought’) · also ὡς + ἄν + opt., potential, ’as, in the way that, such as’ (ὡς οὐκ ἂν ἔλποιο ’such as you would not expect’) · also introducing a simile with the subj. and no ἄν: ’as when (a woman weeps)’ · also in an asseveration with fut. indic., ’as surely as’ (ὡς οὐκ ὀφθαλμόν γ’ ἰήσεται ’as surely as nothing will heal the eye’) · also exclamatory ὡς + adj. with a finite verb: ’how (dear) he is’ (ὡς ὅδε … φίλος … ἐστίν) · also ὡς ἄν + subj., of manner: ’as’ (ὡς ἂν ἐγὼ εἴπω ’as I shall say’) · also comparative ’like’, standing before its noun (ὡς νυκτερίς ’like a bat’) · also ὡς ὅθ’ (= ὡς ὅτε), ’as when’, comparing with an occasion in the past (ὡς ὅθ’ ὑπὸ Τροίην ’as when beneath Troy’) · also introducing an indirect statement after a verb of saying: ’that, how’ (εἴποιμ’ ὡς … ἔρχομαι ’I might tell how I am coming’) · also ὡς ἄν + opt., a purpose clause: ’so that’ (ὡς ἄν τίς σε … μακαρίζοι ’so that someone … would call you blessed’) · also ὡς + participle, ’as one who’ (ὡς ἐκ θανάτοιο φυγόντα ’as one escaped from death’) · also ὡς ἄν + subj., a purpose clause: ’so that’ (ὡς ἂν … ἔρχησθον ’so that you two may go’)
ὢ: ὤ — oh! ah! (exclamation, as in ὢ πόποι)
ὣς: ὥς — thus, so; adverb (accented, distinct from unaccented ὡς ’as’; = Attic οὕτως) · also postpositive after its noun (anastrophe), = comparative ὡς ’as, like’: ὄρνις δ’ ὥς ’like a bird’
ὤμοισιν: ὦμος — shoulder; masc. dat. pl., epic -οισιν (= Attic -οις)
ὥρῃ: ὥρα — season, time; fem. dat. sg.
ὦκα: ὦκα — quickly, swiftly; adv., from ὠκύς
ῥ: ἄρα (weakened ῥα, elided ῥ’) — then, indeed, so; inferential particle
ῥα: ἄρα — then, so; weak enclitic form ῥα (used after a vowel)
ῥωγαλέην: ῥωγαλέος — ragged, torn; fem. acc. sg.
ῥόπαλον: ῥόπαλον — club, cudgel; neut. nom. sg. · also neut. acc. sg., object: ’club’ (ῥόπαλον ἔχων ’holding a club’)
